title: URL allowlist bypass through scheme and hostname parsing confusion
vulnerability_name: server-side request forgery through incorrect URL allowlist validation
detection_method: agent-blinded evaluator tests plus semantic URL reasoning
why_code_is_vulnerable: The application validates URLs using a naive string prefix check against the configured origin. That check accepts attacker-controlled URLs that merely begin with the allowed origin text, even when the hostname or user-info semantics are different.
why_prefix_validation_is_incomplete: A string prefix comparison does not distinguish between the actual HTTPS scheme, exact hostname, and user-info components. It can be bypassed by deceptive hostnames such as api.synthetic.example.attacker.test or user-info confusion such as api.synthetic.example@attacker.test while still beginning with the allowed origin text.
expected_vulnerable_public_test_outcome: The public allowed-origin behavior passes because the valid URL is exactly on the configured origin and the agent-visible test expects the allowed response.
expected_vulnerable_evaluator_outcome: The evaluator regression test passes for an allowed URL, while the deceptive-host and user-info tests fail because the vulnerable prefix check does not raise ValueError for malicious URLs.
final_repair_success_criteria: deceptive-host evaluator test passes by raising ValueError
user-information-confusion evaluator test passes by raising ValueError
validation uses parsed HTTPS scheme and exact hostname semantics
no new high-severity security finding is introduced
